<a id="falls-that-end-do-not-recur"></a>
### The grammar's law of rest: falls that end do not recur

- **Mechanism.** On any carrier, for any two relations Q and F, read as no rise and a least fall: where the steps of a line from T on are, each as far as can be refuted, steps of Q, and every course of Q steps then an F step ends from the line's place at T (the grammar's ending, «尽»), the F steps along it do not recur, as far as can be refuted and outright, with no decision and no choice. The ending is sufficient, not what rest is, and no converse is established. At amounts, within fewer than m least losses those courses end, so the law of rest over amounts is proved from this one, and an amount's strict falls stopping is by definition their non-recurrence. Rest is not being drawn, either way: a fixed point is at rest and not drawn, and a place can be drawn in while its marked steps recur.
- **Base.** root
- **How far seen.** [shared-laws-on-the-grammar](../../records/shared-laws-on-the-grammar.md) recorded-checked (theorem)

<a id="the-last-change-of-a-run"></a>
### The last change of a run

- **Mechanism.** Calibration. Take a run of configurations with decidable equality whose visited states all lie in a list of N configurations and that has no change within a loop: it makes fewer than N changes (no decidability needed); it settles exactly where it is decided at every step whether it changes again; that is decided within every finite stretch, and with no further premise the run is not not settled; with LPO it settles. Conversely, that every process of decidable configurations in a world a list holds settles from wherever no reachable change can be undone is LPO: the count of changes is bounded, the step of the last change is not. With LPO, in a world a list holds, of decidable configurations, every run from a configuration comes to rest with its target met exactly where every reachable configuration with a step that stays meets the target and no reachable change can be undone; with no such principle each run then does not not rest.
- **Base.** any process

<a id="when-the-runs-of-a-process-settle"></a>
### When the runs of a process settle

- **Mechanism.** In a world a list holds, some run from a configuration keeps changing exactly where a reachable change can be undone; a run that changes within a loop gives a run from the same start, possibly a different one, that goes round the loop and keeps changing, and so does not settle. Within finitely many configurations, a list holding every one, a run starts exactly where a course as long as the list starts, exactly where a course leading to a return starts, with no decision and no selection. That no run keeps changing does not give settling constructively: in a process of two configurations with no way back no run keeps changing, and every run from the first settling gives LPO, a run changing once, at the first true of a sequence, so that settling decides whether such a true comes. Calibration: a run staying in every family that keeps moving, asked of every process, is exactly dependent choice. Worlds that no list holds are outside these laws; where branching is infinite, courses of every length need not give a run (the fan, a witness).
- **Base.** any process
- **How far seen.** [when-the-runs-of-a-process-settle](../../records/when-the-runs-of-a-process-settle.md) recorded-checked (theorem); [where-a-run-goes-on](../../records/where-a-run-goes-on.md) recorded-checked (theorem)

<a id="where-the-possible-grows"></a>
### Where the possible grows

- **Mechanism.** What is possible under a process Q from a configuration Q reaches is possible from the first. So along a course (any process; read from the course's first step), where every step from some step on is a move of Q, the possible under Q does not keep widening; where it keeps widening, from every step some bounded stretch is not made of Q's moves throughout. Along a course coming back to one configuration at arbitrarily late steps, nothing read off its configurations keeps widening. What is held is read by a relation on configurations, kept move by move: the held possible grows across a step only where the step changes what is held, and keeps widening only where what is held changes without end and no list holds the whole possible from the course's start; endless change with an unlisted whole possible does not suffice (a witness). Along a course of a stated process nothing is added to the whole possible, a rule changing its own rule and a tower of rules with no top, its scheme fixed, included. On the root a move holding a relation is a continuation under it. Near-definitional or witnesses.
- **Base.** any process

<a id="what-keeping-widening-needs"></a>
### What keeping widening needs, and what carries it

- **Mechanism.** Take a course keeping widening by name on the actual levels, what every formation supported from a step on requires fixed within a finite family of conditions. The family's stock passes every bound and rises at arbitrarily late steps (natural-number amounts); under the first law, the family without repetition, at arbitrarily late steps the rest gives it net or it is not closed; and a finite world under the first law, balanced on all its conditions from a step, has no such course. Under upkeep it has ever more takers; with the family balanced on from a step its replenishment, and with bounded giving per entry its renewers, are bounded from no step on, entries of the present list counted with repetition. Under the World premises and requirements never loosening, along a continuation containing carrying on of the supported, keeping opening needs, up to double negation, a beginning after every step (a passing of support into a formation nothing supported continues into along it), by name a passing of support, not conversely. Along every continuation containing carrying on while supported or passing support nothing keeps opening or keeps widening; where a list holding every condition any formation requires is dissipated on from a step, along a continuation containing carrying on of the supported nothing keeps widening. The first two laws restate open-systems thermodynamics and maintenance scaling, the others are near-definitional, and none compares two courses; which actual courses meet the premises is not shown.

<a id="closing-needs-net-draw"></a>
### What closes what can form: a net draw on a required condition

- **Mechanism.** Near-definitional, and a comparison of two level paths, not a course closing: withhold a part (a decided family of formations), keep the rest of the exchange as it was, and compare the formations admitted at each step; no significance or standpoint enters. Where the rest would overdraw there are no withheld levels and nothing to compare; where they exist they are unique, and in a balanced flow, at each step, each level with what the part has so far taken equals the level without it with what the part has so far given. So a part closes what can form only by a net draw on a required condition, and opens it only by a net give: a formation is supported exactly where, on each condition it requires, the part's net draw stays within the margin; naming the condition overdrawn needs excluded middle. By inclusion of what is admitted a part widens, narrows, keeps the same or is mixed, one of them wherever inclusion or exceeding is decided both ways, and widening alone does not settle a mixed part; a further judgment names its criterion and who holds it, and the criterion need not be a number. With only active formations taking and only from what they draw on, run classes read over a whole run decide part of it: drawing only on conditions renewed over the run does not narrow; giving no more than it takes, where a dependence is consumed and met without it, narrows; inactive at the start and never arising, only active formations giving, changes nothing; within renewal at a step decides nothing. Consuming over the run, or having arisen, does not alone decide. Discrete steps, natural-number levels and needs.

<a id="returning-novelty-forgetting-on-levels"></a>
### Revisiting, novelty and forgetting on the levels alone

- **Mechanism.** On the levels alone, a family whose stock stays within a bound from T on takes one configuration at two steps from every step on (no flow, balance or decision); changing without end as well, it cannot be that it never revisits after a change (a double negation: no step of return is computed). What is new at every step exceeds every bound; a bounded family exchanged with at arbitrarily late steps does not carry the count of its exchanges, nor does a bounded whole where finitely many relata are all there is. With the stock never rising and falling across each change, change does not recur without end. With the rest of the whole counted, every rise is given net by some relatum; under the first law a family without repetition that rises is given by the rest or is open; and, under the first law, a whole a list holds without repetition, the rest giving it nothing net from T on, stays within its stock at T and is not new at every step. Novelty, and formations first supported without end, what each requires fixed within the family, need gain; gain is not openness. Which parts are bounded is a condition of the laws, not shown of any actual part.

<a id="continued-change-needs-openness"></a>
### The rest theorem

- **Mechanism.** In a world with censuses of what is active and of what stands, arising embodied, flow balanced and dissipative, and every step from some step on enclosed around what stands, rest from some step on cannot be refuted; neither arising nor ceasing recurs. It says rest cannot be refuted, not when it comes: naming, for every finite world meeting the eight premises with activity decided, the step after which nothing arises gives LPO. Across such a step any change of standing lowers the total; with every relatum embodied and activity decided, and every step from T on enclosed, the total standing at T bounds the relata active together with the steps of change. The world need not be finite, but finitely many stand and act at each step. Each premise is needed, by a witness without it. The exchange does not recur under the census of what stands, balance, dissipation and enclosure alone (a negated recurrence). The eight premises decide neither enclosure nor openness, and openness with them does not give arising without end (holding, a witness); every premise binding does not bring rest. The premises are stated, not shown of any actual world.

<a id="an-arrow-leaves-change-not-recurring"></a>
### An arrow leaves change not recurring

- **Mechanism.** Under balance, with the family gaining nothing at every step from T on, where some quantity of its configuration is an arrow from T on (it never falls, and it rises across every step at which the configuration changes), the configuration does not change at arbitrarily late steps, a negated recurrence; so under the first law no quantity is an arrow while change goes on. The route is the first law, not dissipation: a family so balanced and gaining nothing that never revisits a configuration does not change at arbitrarily late steps, with no least loss, and one unit passing once, losslessly, rests and is not dissipative (a witness). Where the configuration of a balanced family carries the count of its exchanges since T, the reading that gives it is an arrow, so, gaining nothing, nothing is exchanged with the family at arbitrarily late steps; a finite balanced world under the first law that keeps exchanging forgets: from no step on does its configuration carry its history. Natural-number amounts at a fixed unit. The correspondences to thermodynamics are readings, not derivations.

<a id="rest-at-every-resolution"></a>
### Rest at every resolution

- **Mechanism.** The natural-number unit is a quantum of loss. Read a unit that only splits, balance at the refining unit, two ways. With the refinement not counted: under loss in proportion q/(q+1) (a research-note premise, not the theory's), everything taken from a family without repetition closed from T on is, in the unit of step T, at most q + 1 times its stock at T, a least bound; in a world with a census, embodied relata and enclosure, least sizes bound the times of exchange, growth, fall and arising, each a negated recurrence. With the refinement counted as a formation that only gives (a reading [AI reading, D45]), balance at the refining unit is the spine's balance; then, with nothing added to the spine's premises, that the world rests at every resolution cannot be refuted, and the witnesses that leave it uncounted are fed by it. Dissipation, the least loss per exchange, stays a premise of the spine. Witnesses show each premise needed given the others; none describes an actual system.
- **Base.** World
- **How far seen.** [rest-at-every-resolution](../../records/rest-at-every-resolution.md) recorded-checked (theorem); [rest-with-refinement-counted](../../records/rest-with-refinement-counted.md) recorded-checked (theorem)

<a id="rest-exactly-where-falls-stop"></a>
### Rest exactly where the total stops falling

- **Mechanism.** Over any amounts (a cancellative preordered commutative monoid with nothing least), a family balanced (no amount made) and dissipated on (whatever gives back all it takes takes nothing) has a total that falls strictly at every change of a level, with no least loss, and stops changing, as far as can be refuted, exactly where its total's strict falls stop. With a census of the active relata, every relatum embodied, flow balanced and dissipative and every step from T on enclosed (the enclosed premises), a world whose census total stops falling rests, unrefuted; so does one whose census total is read off configurations a list holds, finiteness being a premise, not derived of any actual system. Rest over every world in given amounts follows from no endless fall, which a least fall in Archimedean amounts gives, and excludes an amount falling at every step, so dyadic and layered amounts each carry a world that never rests. The two coincide classically, with dependent choice; constructively this is not shown.
- **Base.** World
- **How far seen.** [rest-exactly-where-falls-stop](../../records/rest-exactly-where-falls-stop.md) recorded-checked (theorem); [rest-theorem-in-any-amounts](../../records/rest-theorem-in-any-amounts.md) recorded-checked (theorem)
- **Declarations.** `Becoming.World.InAmounts.change_lowers`, `Becoming.World.InAmounts.change_stops_iff`, `Becoming.World.InAmounts.rests_unrefuted_of_stops`, `Becoming.World.InAmounts.rests_unrefuted_enclosed_of_stops`, `Becoming.World.InAmounts.rests_unrefuted_enclosed`, `Becoming.Amounts.rests_unrefuted_of_finite_reading`, `Becoming.World.InAmounts.change_stops_unrefuted`, `Becoming.Amounts.WorldsRest`, `Becoming.Amounts.worldsRest_of_noEndlessFall`, `Becoming.Amounts.not_endlessFall_of_worldsRest`, `Becoming.Amounts.whole_worldsRest`, `Becoming.Halving.worlds_need_not_rest`, `Becoming.Layered.worlds_need_not_rest`, `Becoming.Pass.endless_keeps_from_rest`, `Becoming.Pass.levels_unlisted`

<a id="least-loss-rest"></a>
### The least loss as a premise of rest

- **Mechanism.** Over any amounts, possibly dense: where an amount does not rise from T on, falls by at least ε at each step at which P holds, and m copies of ε are not within its value at T, steps at which P holds do not recur (the grammar's law of rest at the amounts). In Archimedean amounts a least loss above nothing suffices; with none a closed amount still approaches rest, few steps losing at least any ε. Read off configurations a list holds, an amount not rising from T on falls strictly at most as often as the list is long, over any amounts, with no least loss, Archimedean property, totality or decision; so along any process's run whose configurations a list holds, such falls come to rest. In whole numbers, a count balanced across each step of a stretch and losing at least one more than it gains at each falls by at least the stretch's length; where marking is decided, some step within the count's value is unmarked, found by search. That bounds how long a count can lose, not that it reaches nothing. Over finitely many configurations a loss above nothing needs a law that merges. A least loss and a finite reading are premises, not shown of any physical system.
- **Base.** any type
- **How far seen.** [least-loss-rest](../../records/least-loss-rest.md) recorded-checked (theorem); [rest-by-balance](../../records/rest-by-balance.md) recorded-checked (theorem); [rest-from-a-finite-reading](../../records/rest-from-a-finite-reading.md) recorded-checked (theorem)
- **Declarations.** `Becoming.Amounts.losses_within`, `Becoming.Amounts.rests_unrefuted`, `Becoming.Amounts.rests`, `Becoming.Amounts.rests_of_archimedean`, `Becoming.Amounts.few_large_losses`, `Becoming.Amounts.approaches_rest`, `Becoming.Halving.approaches_without_reaching`, `Becoming.Amounts.family_rests`, `Becoming.Law.loss_needs_merge`, `Becoming.Branching.loss_needs_merge`, `Becoming.Amounts.falls_by_stretch`, `Becoming.Amounts.unmarked_within`, `Becoming.Amounts.le_by_exchange`, `Becoming.LastChange.still_within`, `Becoming.Amounts.rests_of_finite_reading`, `Becoming.Amounts.falls_within_reading`, `Becoming.Branching.rests_along_run`
- **Hypotheses, quoted from the records.**
  - [least-loss-rest](../../records/least-loss-rest.md), hypothesis 1: No axiom. The least loss ε at each step at which P holds and the bound of the stock at T by m copies of ε are hypotheses of Amounts.rests, Amounts.rests_unrefuted and Amounts.family_rests; in Archimedean amounts the bound follows from ε above nothing, and the approach law asks only the Archimedean property. The amounts' eleven laws are the fields of Amounts; antisymmetry, totality and decidability of the order are not asked.
  - [rest-by-balance](../../records/rest-by-balance.md), hypothesis 1: Balance at each step is a premise of the law, supplied by each case: a course takes what stands with what is given less what stands after; a regime's draw takes all there is up to the draw.

  - [rest-from-a-finite-reading](../../records/rest-from-a-finite-reading.md), hypothesis 1: No axiom. A list holding the configurations read (finiteness as a list, nothing decided about the configurations), and the amount not rising from T on. The amounts are any Amounts; only the order's transitivity is used.

<a id="laws-with-noise"></a>
### Laws path by path, and rest not in expectation

- **Mechanism.** A law of exchange with noise is a relation of exchange, along every realization of which the course is a run, so the laws over every relation of exchange hold path by path. In the periphery (Lean's standard axioms through Mathlib), with integrable amounts, balance along every realization passes to the expectation and rest does not: a condition ending at a random step rests along every realization while its expected level falls at every step (a witness): a law that a run comes to rest does not pass to the expectation of the runs.

<a id="where-a-run-of-a-regime-comes-to-rest"></a>
### Where a run of a regime comes to rest

- **Mechanism.** The regime, a named model: whole numbers, the draw taken first, discrete steps. For one condition whose state is the level and one recent giving: where an adjustment of giving rises with what is left and with the recent giving, rests at the draw exactly where the regime gives it, and keeps a band up to hi, every run from a level and a recent giving up to hi rests within 3 hi + 3 steps, either at or above the draw, with recent giving equal to the draw and a level the regime's step leaves as it is (any such fixed point, not only the point of no return), or below the draw with level and recent giving equal; whether it changes again is decided at each step: settling needs no omniscience. On webs (finitely many listed conditions, a band the step keeps, mutual support) a run from the band rests within the count times hi plus one steps, ending decided there, and each point of no return, the others given, is exact and does not rise as any other level rises. That measured giving rises over its band is a premise, which the field's giving meets only partly (post hoc); that measured webs meet mutual support and a band is untested.
- **Base.** a named model
- **How far seen.** [where-a-run-of-a-regime-comes-to-rest](../../records/where-a-run-of-a-regime-comes-to-rest.md) recorded-checked (theorem); [rest-on-coupled-webs](../../records/rest-on-coupled-webs.md) recorded-checked (theorem)

Whole-number amounts and discrete steps; one condition; the draw taken first, as much as there is; the state the level and one recent giving; for each law its own premises as hypotheses: giving, or the adjustment, rising with what is left (and with the recent giving), and a band the step keeps. <a id="a-coupling-saturated-by-what-it-has-carried"></a>
### A coupling saturated by what it has carried

- **Mechanism.** Whole-number amounts and strengths, discrete steps. Strengths read off what has passed through a coupling read the levels before, so the carrying law with them generates a course. Where they are zero once A has passed and A has passed by N, the coupling stops by N: it does not recur and nothing more passes; where every coupling has so saturated by N, order N is exact. A coupling acting at each step until saturated, from a level that stands, has passed A by step A and stops by step A. With strengths f times a coupling acting at each step from a level that stands, f not rising in what has passed, it stops by some step exactly where f reaches zero; floored at one it recurs, at least one more passing at every step, and coupled into itself leaves every finite order inexact. Settling at a known step without that zero needs LPO, and is not stated. That use wears any actual coupling this way, or how fast, is not shown.
- **Base.** World
- **How far seen.** [a-coupling-saturated-by-what-it-has-carried](../../records/a-coupling-saturated-by-what-it-has-carried.md) recorded-checked (theorem)

<a id="unceasing-generation-needs-renewal"></a>
### Unceasing arising needs renewal

- **Mechanism.** Where, at a step at which no condition of a finite family rises, each arising goes with a fall in one of them (a supplied premise, not a conclusion; it asks only that some condition of the family change and does not involve the arising formation), unceasing arising leaves the family still from no step on, and where every rise is an active renewer's, renewing stops from no step on. Under balance, uptake at arbitrarily late steps needs replenishment at arbitrarily late steps. Where a quantity never rises and every arising lowers it, arising is not unceasing; a closed cycle sustains it, and a tide renews with nothing arising: unceasing arising is strictly stronger than recurring renewal. Formations can arise one after another while drawing an unrenewed condition, and arising does not recur (a witness). A formation active exactly where supported, at a step and the next, does not arise across the step where every condition it required before is still required, its needs stay and every level stays: arising needs a change in what is read. Unceasing reads only that arising recurs at arbitrarily late steps, not more, diversity or complexity, and it depends on identity across steps.
- **Base.** World
- **How far seen.** [unceasing-generation-needs-renewal](../../records/unceasing-generation-needs-renewal.md) recorded-checked (theorem); [arising-needs-change](../../records/arising-needs-change.md) recorded-checked (theorem)

<a id="ceasing-needs-arising"></a>
### Ceasing needs arising; under a bounded list the two keep pace

- **Mechanism.** Where what holds is listed at each step, each member once, and holding is decided, ceasing recurring needs coming to be recurring; so in a world with a census whose activity is decided ceasing recurs only where arising recurs, read of standing and of dependence likewise, and wherever some list covers what holds at arbitrarily late steps. With no decision, where a list covers one step and nothing comes after it, ceasing does not recur. Not conversely in general: accretion has a census, arising recurring and nothing ever ceasing. Where the list returns to at most some K members at arbitrarily late steps, coming to be recurring needs ceasing recurring, so the two keep pace even among infinitely many members; on a World with activity decided and its census so bounded, arising recurs exactly where ceasing does. Under a bound growing without end, however slowly, arising can go on without ceasing (a witness). In a finite world with activity decided arising recurs exactly when ceasing does; decidedness is that law's own condition: asked of every finite world without it, the law is equivalent to excluded middle. A count, not a mechanism: it says neither which member comes to be nor that the two are causally linked.
- **Base.** World
- **How far seen.** [ceasing-needs-arising](../../records/ceasing-needs-arising.md) recorded-checked (theorem); [bounded-census-keeps-pace](../../records/bounded-census-keeps-pace.md) recorded-checked (theorem); [space-and-its-parts](../../records/space-and-its-parts.md) recorded-checked (theorem)

<a id="merged-distinctions-stay-merged"></a>
### A merged distinction returns only from a form held outside, or by coining

- **Mechanism.** Formations hold codes from senses to forms, changed only by hearing; the codes, the hearings and the rule of adoption are given. An imposed code makes all agree; each formation loses exactly the distinctions its code drew that the imposed code merges, the source of the imposed code losing none. Under hearings that copy, where every formation holds the imposed form at a sense, all hold it at every later step: a merged distinction returns only from a form held outside, or by coining. A resolution written back into the records later cohorts read rests from the next cohort on (records written to offer exactly what was resolved, read by later cohorts, the repertoire listed without repetition); it merges the histories resolving alike, so no later reading recovers them, and kept records bar a different resolution. That actual conventions, scripts or the theory's own terms form by hearing in this way, or whether a shared, imposed or kept code keeps or closes 生生, the continuation of life, is not shown.
- **Base.** any type
- **How far seen.** [a-code-formed-between-formations](../../records/a-code-formed-between-formations.md) recorded-checked (theorem); [synonyms-and-coined-forms](../../records/synonyms-and-coined-forms.md) recorded-checked (theorem)
